name: Briseis Mwangi-Castellano
description: A Shelf-born spoken word performer and visual agitator operating out of the Caldwell Underpass arts pocket in the southern Shelf districts, Briseis Mwangi-Castellano — known on the street as 'Bris' or simply 'the Mouth' — delivers raw political commentary through BCI-broadcast poetry injected directly into open neural feeds without subscriber gates. Her performances layer live vocal delivery with illegal signal-burst visuals that hijack nearby public ad-screens for thirty-second intervals, turning corporate displays into her canvas. She has never accepted a corporate residency, a fact she repeats in every broadcast.
cultural_impact: Her open-gate neural broadcasts reach an estimated 400,000 unsubscribed listeners per session, making her one of the few voices in M88 who can claim a genuinely un-monetized mass audience. Shelf residents frequently quote her lines as shorthand for political positions in ways that bypass corporate surveillance keyword filters.
locations: Caldwell Underpass Arts Pocket, South Shelf
story_hooks: A Tier 4 media corponation offers Bris an unprecedented fully-uncensored contract — and someone needs to figure out whether it's genuine or a trap to silence her through co-option.
One of her signal-burst hijacks accidentally reveals a corporate data packet embedded in a public ad-screen, and now both she and Piotr are being hunted by people who want that data erased.
A young Shelf kid claims Briseis's voice saved them from a gang induction — and now that kid is missing, and Bris feels responsible.
platform: Open Neural Feed (unsubscribed BCI broadcast) + illegal ad-screen hijack visuals
follower_count: ~400K active listeners per session, no formal subscriber count
controversy: In 2214 she broadcast a 40-minute piece naming three specific Vantec-Meridian middle managers by full legal name and residential address, accusing them of ordering the demolition of a Shelf housing block while residents were still inside. The corponation filed seventeen injunctions. All seventeen were dismissed on procedural grounds — a fact she has broadcast no fewer than twelve times since.
